_why: 2026-08-02, security scan finding (HIGH x2). Flow ships two native binaries it
does not build: the whisper speech engine and WinKeyServer.exe, the process that
watches every keystroke on the machine. Both were fetched from third-party GitHub
repositories with NO integrity check at all, and one of them resolved 'latest'
The attack was not hypothetical and it did not need Flow to be compromised at all.
Someone who took over the upstream account publishes a trojaned asset; the next
time a v* tag is pushed here, CI downloads it, packages it, and - this is the part
that stings - the build-provenance attestation added the day before faithfully
signs the result as a genuine Flow build. Every install auto-updates. The malicious
binary is then spawned as the speech engine, or IS the keyboard hook.
Pinning a VERSION is not enough on its own: GitHub lets a release asset be replaced
in place, so a tag names a file, never its bytes. Only a hash names the bytes.
TO UPDATE ONE OF THESE: change the version, run scripts/verify-native-deps.cjs
--print to get the new hashes, and commit them in the SAME change. A hash bump
without a version bump, or the reverse, is what this file exists to make visible
